newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean tycoon in loans scandal hospitalised.
newsitem.headline: South Korean tycoon in loans scandal hospitalised.

text.p: The arrested founder of South Korea's Hanbo Group, who is at the centre of a loans scandal, was taken to hospital from a jail on Tuesday after complaining of dizziness, a prison official said.

Chung Tae-soo is on trial on bribery and other charges along with nine others, including three close associates of President Kim Young-sam, in connection with the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co, flagship of the country's 14th largest conglomerate.
State prosecutors charge that Chung bribed politicians and bankers to keep loans rolling into Hanbo Steel, which collapsed in January under debts of $5.8 billion.
They alleged that Chung diverted millions of dollars from the bank loans earmarked for investment and used the money to buy influence from politicians and bankers.
The Hanbo founder and his aides have told prosecutors that they gave money to 33 politicians as "political funds" but denied bribing them, according to senior prosecutor Shim Je-ryoon.
More than 10 prominent politicians, including two tipped as possible candidates of the ruling New Korea Party in presidential elections due in December, have been questioned by the prosecution.
Among the 33 politicians are 20 lawmakers, 13 from the ruling party.
